name: Vauchamps

art.title: Prussian infantry at Étoges, during Vauchamps

summary: Blücher, coming on with Kleist's and Kapzevich's corps against Marmont, met Napoleon instead; Grouchy's cavalry rode round the retreating allied squares, which fought their way back through the French horsemen to Étoges with heavy loss.

sources.label: Six Days' Campaign order of battle (Wikipedia)

toCome.name: Marmont's Corps
toCome.formation: Lagrange's 3rd and Ricard's 8th Divisions, VI Corps
toCome.summary: Ricard's division attacked Zieten's brigade in Vauchamps; Lagrange's followed the retreat and took Étoges after dark.

toCome.name: Grouchy's Cavalry
toCome.summary: Rode round Zieten's flank and cut off his retreat, then charged again and again at the allied squares as they fell back along the road; Doumerc's cuirassiers surprised Udom's Russians at Étoges in the night.

toCome.name: Nansouty's Guard Cavalry
toCome.formation: Lefebvre-Desnouettes's and Laferrière's Guard Cavalry Divisions
toCome.summary: Pressed Zieten's left as Grouchy came round his right.

toCome.name: Friant's Old Guard
toCome.summary: Marched up behind the cavalry; only one battalion came into action.

toCome.name: Kleist's Corps
toCome.formation: Pirch's 10th, Zieten's 11th and Prince August's 12th Brigades, II Corps, Army of Silesia
toCome.summary: About thirteen thousand five hundred men. Zieten's brigade, caught at Vauchamps, lost two thousand prisoners, and the corps fought its way back to Étoges in squares through the French cavalry; Kleist and Prince August were nearly taken.

toCome.name: Kaptsevich's Corps
toCome.formation: X Infantry Corps, Army of Silesia
toCome.summary: About six thousand five hundred men, falling back beside Kleist's; Urusov's 8th Division, left at Étoges, was taken there with eight guns.

toCome.name: Udom's Division
toCome.summary: The fifteen hundred who had got away from Champaubert, surprised at Étoges after dark by Doumerc's cuirassiers.
